description: BSuite shared Supabase project migration scopes. Parent bsuite is the control-plane repo; app repos and packages may still own their local migrations.

scopes.label: R80.4
scopes.note: R80.4 owned NO database objects when it replaced R80.3 in the applier matrix on 2026-08-06, and this entry carried has_database:false to record that the absence was deliberate rather than a missing path. That stopped being true on 2026-08-12, when R80.4 shipped its first migration (20260814010000_r80_saved_quotes.sql — 'R80.4's save is device-local'). The flag was flipped and migrations_dir added on 2026-08-12 by the migration-rehearsal lane, which found the drift because it refused to trust the manifest over the filesystem. The live applier (supabase-migrate.yml) was never affected — it tests for the directory on disk — but plan-preview-db.mjs reads THIS file, so the preview plan silently understated the blast radius of every R80.4 change. A capability flag is a claim about the world, and the world moves: scripts/supabase/rehearse-migrations.mjs now warns when any scope declares has_database:false while carrying migrations on disk.

scopes.label: Schema Builder package
scopes.dev_fixture_note: DEV-FIXTURE COPIES, not a migration set the applier runs. The canonical files live in business-suite-unified/supabase/migrations and .github/workflows/schema-builder-migration-parity.yml keeps the SQL below the @sync-boundary-below marker byte-identical. Flagging these as version collisions reports the very duplication another gate is enforcing.

notes: Native Supabase branching only sees the connected GitHub repository working directory. Keep parent bsuite as the control plane.
For app-repo PRs, add a repository_dispatch bridge to parent bsuite or rely on parent submodule bump PRs to exercise the full migration manifest.
Vite apps must receive VITE_* Supabase aliases in Vercel previews; Supabase/Vercel integrations commonly inject NEXT_PUBLIC_* names.

retired_scopes.label: R80.3 (archived 2026-08-06)
retired_scopes.why_it_still_matters: Its 31 migrations are APPLIED to the shared project and their versions remain permanently occupied in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations. The applier keys on the 14-digit version alone, so a NEW migration in any live scope that reuses one of these stamps is silently skipped forever. Any duplicate-stamp check MUST keep scanning the archived path.
